full_judgment:
3.1. The suit property measuring 48 decimals of land appertaining to CS Khatin No. 1539 was originally recorded in the names of Shashi Mohan and his four (04) brothers in equal shares. The same land was recorded in SA Khatian Nos. 1828 and 1948 comprising of 34 decimals and 14 decimals respectively in the lone name of Dhirendra Mohan Dey, the son of Sree Sasi Mohan Dey. Thereafter, recent B.R.S Khatian No. 5023 was finally published incorporating the said suit land in the name of Abdul Aziz, the predecessor of writ petitioner Nos. 2-8 and Md. Zoynal Abedin, petitioner No. 01. Regarding the suit land, relevant government authority instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 40 of 1974 for correction of BRS Khatian No. 5023 and Abdul Aziz and Zoynal Abedin instituted Other Classes Suit No. 136 of 1976 for declaration of title to the said land. Both suits were disposed of analogously by the then Subordinate Judge, Mymensingh vide judgment dated 31-5-1977 decreeing the Other Classes Suit in part declaring plaintiffs' title to 1 anna 12 gondas only of the suit land and the rest to be in the category of enemy property and thereupon, ordering to correct the BRS Khatian No. 5023 accordingly in the name of relevant government authority. The decree dated 31-5-1977 was challenged by the plaintiffs before the High Court Division in Appeal No. 74 of 1977 which due to establishment of Arpito Sampotti Prottarpon Tribunal under the Arpito Sampotti Prottarpon Ain, 2001 got abated in view of section 13 of the Ain. Be it noted, the entire quantum of suit land has been enlisted as vested property in Schedule-Ka vide gazette notification published on 9-4-2012. 

 4.1. There was no reason to enlist the suit land as vested property as the petitioners have been althrough in peaceful possession thereof since 1975. The entire quantum of the suit land belonged to Dhirendra Mohan Dey by means of amicable partition amongst the co-sharers and, consequently, the Khatian No. 1948 and 1828 were published in his sole name. Dhirendra Mohan Dey transferred vide two registered sale deeds dated 1-10-1975 bearing No. 25175 and dated 5-11-1975 bearing No. 28129 incorporating 34 decimals and 14 decimals respectively in favour of the predecessors of these petitioners. Post-transfer necessary legal actions including mutation and payment of up to date land tax, holding tax etc. have been duly completed; even BRS Khatian No. 5023 also has been correctly prepared and published in the names of the recipients of the sale deeds. Those deeds and updated Khatian are still in force in petitioners' favour. They are the real owners or 'malik' of the land in question and the government authority never had possession in and control over the land by virtue of any title vested in it. Resorting to tricky device some colourable lease documents have been created and a sham lease has been shown to have been granted in favour of one Laxmi Rani, who, in fact, had been the tenant under Dhirendra Mohan Dey. The suit land during recent revisional survey was recorded in khas Khatian No. 01 which upon being challenged by the petitioners under Rule 30 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 was ordered to be released from khash Khatian and to open separate khatians also in their names. The tribunal or the appellate tribunal without appreciation of evidence adduced, whether documentary or testimonial, in its appropriate perspective, dismissed the Arpito Sampotti Prottarpon Case and the appeal upon misconception of law. Hence, both the judgments and the decrees passed by both the tribunal and appellate tribunal as mentioned hereinabove are nullity and are liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. 

 6.1. First of all, petitioner's learned counsel Mr. Md. Bodruddoza, referring to an undisposed of local inspection application by the tribunal, submits that the same was brought to substantiate the existence of petitioners' having buildings on the suit land but neither of the tribunals below, trial or appellate, ever addressed the said application or the aspect of petitioners' possession over the suit land, rather both the tribunals disbelieved the factum of possession despite stronger basis thereof remaining present. The learned counsel further submits that the positive evidence of possession, both oral and documentary, .appearing in the testimonies of PW 1 and PW 2 was not appropriately analyzed in the judgments in its correct approach. The learned counsel emphasizes that the tribunal deliberately skipped DWI 's failure to substantiate government's case on evidence. He also underscores that unnecessarily emphasizing more on the CS Khatian while SA Khatian was finally published in 1962 in petitioners' predecessors favour was a futile and an uncalled for exercise. Since under the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance, 1965, government was only vested with the power of controlling the abandoned property, no title or ownership was created in favour of the government in respect of the vested and non-resident property. The learned counsel underscores that since the suit land has finally been published in BRS Khatian in the names of the petitioners, its inclusion in the vested property in 'Ka' scheduled list is a blatant illegality and a manifest indicia of executive high-handedness. Be it mentioned that the Government also lost in the proceedings under Rule 30 and 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and the title deeds dated 1-10-1975 and 5-11-1975 cited by petitioners in the avbove proceedings were relied on upon by the survey authority. The learned counsel reiterates that petitioners' title document, being duly registered kabalas unless cancelled by competent Court and, a variety of legal documents of possession including finally published khatian and payment of land tax and holding tax etc. were adequate inter-woven evidence to pass an order of releasing the suit land from the impugned vested property list. But the tribunal and the appellate tribunal upon misconception of facts and of law concurrently arrived at a fallacious decisions which are liable to be set-aside. Learned counsel further submits that a construction plan has already been approved by proper authority at the instance of this petitioners upon a certain quantum of suit land. The learned counsel submits that Dhirendra Mohon Dey died in Bangladesh, and since then the petitioners have been in peaceful possession of the suit land by mutating their names and on payment of up to date rent to the government. It is stated that during enjoyment of peaceful possession of the predecessor of the petitioners, Abdul Aziz transferred certain quantum of land to petitioner No. 4 by way of registered sale deed bearing No 12363 of 1992 and thereafter, petitioner No. 04 by mutating his name has been paying rent to government regularly and enjoying its peaceful and uninterrupted possession therein. Learned counsel further submits that after the death of Abdul Aziz (predecessor of the petitioners), petitioner No. 08 inherited some quantum of land from the suit land as per his share and after having inherited the same he also has been enjoying peaceful possession and ownership by mutating his name and paying rent regularly. In view of the above facts and features of the circumstances, the learned counsel, however, urges the Rule to make absolute. 

 6.2. Per contra, Mr. Md. Mohaddes-ul-Islam, learned Deputy Attorney-General on being assisted by Mr. Ashique Rubaiat, learned Assistant Attorney-General, frankly submits on behalf of respondent No. 01 that the SA Khatian in the lone name of Dhirendra Mohon Dey to the extent of whole of suit land and the subsequent BRS Khatian in the names of the petitioners have been wrongly prepared and published. The alleged deeds of sale dated 1-10-1975 and 5-11-1975 did not operate to create title to petitioners' predecessors or to the instant petitioners, as the case may be, to the extent of entire suit land; it only creates title in respect of Dhirendra Mohon Dey's proportionate share of 12 gondas only. Thus petitioners' claim to the entire 48 decimals of suit land does not bear any basis but a ficticin simpliciter. The Deputy Attorney-General further submits that in the case before tribunal the petitioner intentionally concealed the lineage of CS recorded tenants simply for apprehension of losing in the case. The learned counsel concludes that the tribunal upon detailed evidence and hearing disposed of and dismissed the Arpi to Sampotti Prottarpon Case No. 75 of 2013 which had been rightly affirmed in appeal. 

 7.2. It, however, appears that the tribunal while adjudicating the contentions raised in the Arpito Sampotti Tribunal Case held, Annexure-B-3, that the petitioners were not entitled to acquire title to the whole of suit land since their vendor, Dhirendra Mohon Dey, had no title to the whole amount of land as there were other co-sharers also as per CS Khatian. We find a specific case to have been demonstrated by the petitioners that Dhirendra Mohon Dey by way of amicable partition owned the suit land in the whole. Admitted publication of SA Khatian Nos. 1948 and 1828 in Dhirendra Mohon's single name including the suit land in its entirety excluding other co-sharers therein appeared to be prima facie evidence of his possession at the relevant time. None of the co-sharers ever challenged the correctness of the SA Khatians or the validity of the family partition as being never done by them. It is evident from the impugned Gazette dated 9-4-2012 that the suit property was enlisted as enemy property vide Case No. 71/6970. Till 1969-70, no other co-sharers came forward to resist the claim of Dhirendra Mohon and to refute sole possession of 48 decimals of CS recorded land in Dhirendra Mohon's name alone. But before the enemy list was done, the SA Khatian got finally published attributing thereto the presumption of possession in Dhirendra Mohon's favour. The incorporation of suit land in SA Khatians in Dhirendra Mohon's name reflects the initial basis of amicable family partition particularly when the Khatians continued to operate till further Khatian under new survey operation was published in ultimate conformity with the earlier Khatians. It appears from the lower court record that a number of co-sharers of Dhirendra Mohon Dey were impleaded as defendants in the Other Classes Suit No. 136 of 1976 which was analogously disposed of with Miscellaneous Case No. 40 of 1974. None of the co-sharers entered appearance to resist the family partition claim raised by Dhirendra Mohon Dey, rather impliedly allowed by their unopposed acts being ever raised in any legal action whatsoever. Unless a claim is controverted by persons directly affected or likely to be affected thereby, particularly when such claim is adjudicated with opportunities being provided to all concerned, such claim cannot be unilaterally deprecated on a mere hypothesis unattended by necessary surrounding circumstances. The exclusive and continued possession of one co-sharer over the land of other co-sharers for an unobjected and uninterrupted period of 12 years or more creates title by adverse possession in favour of the co-sharer possessing the land of such other co-sharers without material opposition. In the premises, the decision held either by learned erstwhile Subordinate Judge, Mymensingh in the said analogous judgment of Miscellaneous Case No. 40 of 1974 and Other Classes Suit No. 136 of 1976 or the decision held by the trial tribunal (Annexure-B-3) in Arpito Sampatti Case No. 75 of 2013 or by the appellate tribunal, (Annexure-B-1), in Arpito Appeal No. 02 of 2018, whichever may be, that the basis of SA Khatians in the sole name of Dhirendra Mohon Dey to be absolutely wrong do not appear to us to be in any way logically acceptable. 

 7.3. On the contrary, contesting respondent No. 01 states in the affidavit-in-opposition that only the respective share of Shailendra Mohon Dey to the extent of 12 gondas of suit land was considered as evacuee property after his migration to India with family members after the partition of India in 1947. The respondent althrough assailed to impair the credibility of the title of Dhirendra Mahon Dey as well as that of the petitioners claiming through Dhirendra Mohon relating to suit land but the respondent undertook no effort as to how, when and in what manner the government acquired title to the entire suit land or how that land of 48 decimals came under the control and management of the government. We are unable to detect any full-fledged legal proceedings at government's instance to claim the suit land, except the reference to the case bearing No. 71/69-70 appearing in the relevant column (No. 02) of the impugned Gazette notification dated 9-4-2012. The existence of registered title deeds dated 1-10-1975 and 5-11-1975 (Annexure-D and E), comprising of the suit land in petitioners'/their predecessor's name, the preparation and final publication of BRS Khatian No. 5023 in the names of the recipients of theses deeds (Annexure-G), acknowledge-ment of land tax, (Annexure-I-I series), and holding tax, (Annexure-M series), by the government, the striking out of the suit land from khas Khatian No. 01 and ordering the same to be recorded in separate Khatian in petitioners' name (Annexure-F), etc, are not liable to be knocked down by a simple and solitary assertion of fact that the suit land had been rightly included in the vested property list.
